current_row.boundary_rationale: A paired hoy onset opens the row at “Woe to him who strives with his Maker- a clay pot among the clay pots of the earth!” (web:Isa.45.9), spliced at ה֗וֹי רָ֚ב אֶת יֹ֣צְר֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.45.9, byte tier), matched immediately by the second woe “Woe to him who says to a father, 'What have you become the father of?'” (web:Isa.45.10), spliced at ה֛וֹי אֹמֵ֥ר לְאָ֖ב (oshb:Isa.45.10, byte tier) -- two verse-initial hoy onsets read as one twinned unit rather than split into separate woes, just ahead of the koh-amar reply that opens web:Isa.45.11.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading splits the potter-clay woe of Isa.45.9 from the parent-child woe of Isa.45.10 as two separate one-verse units, since each opens on its own hoy exclamation.
current_row.literature_type_guess: twinned woe-oracle challenging the creature who disputes with its Maker
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: The two hoy sayings are held as one unit on the strength of their shared potter/parent creator-metaphor and their both standing between the same pair of koh-amar frames on either side; a split at Isa.45.9|Isa.45.10 is the disclosed alternative.

items.claim: The row holds two independently-marked woe onsets as one unit at confidence high while a span-internal section mark stands at exactly the disclosed rival's split point, and the prose nowhere discloses that the tier-3 layer runs against the merge.
items.proposed_change: Field repair: disclose in device_notes that the parashah layer divides the pair at the row's internal 45:9|45:10 point and so argues for the disclosed rival, and step confidence from high to medium with frontier_flag_considered set true, matching the neighbour row's handling of the same situation. No respan proposed.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived both ways. MT 45:9 opens ה֗וֹי רָ֚ב אֶת יֹ֣צְר֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.45.9, byte tier) and MT 45:10 opens ה֛וֹי אֹמֵ֥ר לְאָ֖ב (oshb:Isa.45.10, byte tier): two verse-initial tokens of skeleton הוי (skeleton tier; sweep: 22 verses book-wide, count object: skeleton token, verse count; the only ch-45 sites are these two, both verse-initial), and both sit in the book's woe-oracle-onset class, so the disclosed split rival rests on a tier-1 onset signal at 45:10, which the row itself concedes ('each opens on its own hoy exclamation'). Mark inventory (MT keys, single witness): SAMEKH at MT 45:7, 45:8, 45:9 and 45:10, nothing at 45:11, PE at 45:13 -- the SAMEKH after 45:9 falls inside the row's span at exactly the rival's split point, leaving each woe its own section in that layer. The row lists all three marks in boundary_evidence_refs but its prose engages none of them, sets confidence high and frontier_flag_considered false, while the preceding book-order row meets the same shape (SAMEKH after MT 45:7 backing its isolate-45:8 rival) at medium with the flag set: the calibration is inconsistent within the run. The row's merge warrant is byte-true as far as it goes -- both woes stand between the verse-initial frames כֹּה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ (oshb:Isa.45.1, byte tier) and כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְיֹצְר֑וֹ (oshb:Isa.45.11, byte tier) -- and the merge is a legitimate reading under the hybrid granularity rule against per-woe fragmentation, so this is no boundary defect and no respan is warranted. But confidence is a warrant-level claim with governance consequences (band-driven sidecar and frontier handling), and 'high' against an acknowledged tier-1 rival signal plus an undisclosed internal section mark is a defective claim, not a merely mechanical one; the missing prose disclosure compounds it. Medium confirmed; the proposed disclosure in device_notes plus the step to medium with the flag set is the right cure.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The address turns to imperative summons at “Assemble yourselves and come. Draw near together, you who have escaped from the nations.” (web:Isa.45.20), spliced at הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ הִֽתְנַגְּשׁ֥וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו פְּלִיטֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם (oshb:Isa.45.20, byte tier) -- a fresh addressee (the nations' survivors) taking up the declare-and-witness imperative pair הַגִּ֣ידוּ וְהַגִּ֔ישׁוּ (oshb:Isa.45.21, byte tier), “Declare and present it...Who has shown this from ancient time?” (web:Isa.45.21), whose skeleton matches the same imperative pair opening the earlier trial speeches at Isa.41.22 and Isa.41.23 (sweep: 6 verses book-wide carry that shared skeleton). The universal appeal “Look to me, and be saved, all the ends of the earth” (web:Isa.45.22) runs to the closing verdict “All the offspring of Israel will be justified in Yahweh, and will rejoice!” (web:Isa.45.25), the row's own closing verse; the next verse opens a different subject with the ordinary burden noun מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier), not one of the verse-initial oracle headers.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading keeps this summons joined to the self-declaration of Isa.45.18-Isa.45.19 as one extended trial speech rather than cutting a fresh unit at the imperative address to the nations' survivors.
current_row.literature_type_guess: trial speech summoning the nations to a universal turning toward Yahweh

current_row.device_notes: The imperative summons to the nations' survivors is read as the row's own closing trial speech rather than folded into the self-declaration before it, on the strength of its fresh addressee and its own declare-and-witness vocabulary; no marked-division disclosure applies within this span or at its own front seam (0 marked verses across the row's own span).

The pair הַגִּ֣ידוּ וְהַגִּ֔ישׁוּ (oshb:Isa.45.21, byte tier; tokens 1-2 of 23) stands in 1 verse book-wide, Isa.45.21. Not load-bearing: the front seam rests on הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ הִֽתְנַגְּשׁ֥וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו פְּלִיטֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם (oshb:Isa.45.20, byte tier), which re-collates. Confirm at medium.

current_row.boundary_rationale: This row opens on Babylon's own gods collapsing: “Bel bows down. Nebo stoops. Their idols are carried by animals, and on the livestock. The things that you carried around are heavy loads, a burden for the weary.” (web:Isa.46.1) sets the idols of Bel and Nebo onto pack animals as dead weight, their load named with the ordinary carrying-noun מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier) -- a burden common noun in this idol-procession scene, not a verse-initial oracle header of the massa series. The same noun recurs as the idols themselves cannot rescue what they carry: “They stoop and they bow down together. They could not deliver the burden, but they have gone into captivity.” (web:Isa.46.2), spliced at מַלֵּ֣ט מַשָּׂ֑א (oshb:Isa.46.2, byte tier) -- the burden noun here matching Isa.46.1's at accent-stripped tier only, not byte (tipcha there against etnachta here) -- closing the tableau on their own captivity. Two root-level devices bridge into the following verses that an English gloss alone would leave undisclosed: the load-bearer participles נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם עֲמוּס֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.46.1) answered by הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ מִנִּי בֶ֔טֶן הַנְּשֻׂאִ֖ים מִנִּי רָֽחַם (oshb:Isa.46.3) -- disjoint under consonantal search, the plene and defective spellings each standing in exactly 1 verse at skeleton tier, so the tie is root-level and not a form recurrence -- and the rescue root at Isa.46.2 answered by וַאֲמַלֵּֽט (oshb:Isa.46.4), skeleton tier (sweep: 7 verses book-wide). Neither device is treated as reason enough to hold this tableau and the following address in one unit, since web:Isa.46.3 turns the discourse from third-person description to a first-person vocative with a named addressee, the stronger seam signal here.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading merges this tableau with the divine carry-claim that follows at Isa.46.3-Isa.46.4, since the same carry/bear root spans both, but the fresh vocative address at Isa.46.3 is read as the stronger boundary signal.

Isa.45.25 appears in neither the prose nor boundary_evidence_refs (verified against the shipped list), leaving the preceding close בַּיהוָ֛ה יִצְדְּק֥וּ וְיִֽתְהַלְל֖וּ כָּל זֶ֥רַע יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.45.25, byte tier) uncharacterised. The seam is sound on the onset bytes, so the defect is a byte-unengaged, one-edged warrant rather than a boundary defect; the pointed-splice mandate for boundary-relevant claims makes it more than a mechanical shortfall. Confirm at medium.

readjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes at MT 45:25|46:1, both sides. Preceding unit's close: בַּיהוָ֛ה יִצְדְּק֥וּ וְיִֽתְהַלְל֖וּ כָּל זֶ֥רַע יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.45.25, tier: byte), a six-token third-person verdict closing the trial speech, its runs at exactly 1 verse book-wide at skeleton tier -- no refrain, no closing formula, so the refrain-close rule (§6) gives no close-side warrant; the single-witness inventory carries PE at MT 45:17, nothing at MT 45:18-46:1, SAMEKH at 46:2 (absence not counterevidence). Onset side: כָּרַ֥ע בֵּל֙ קֹרֵ֣ס נְב֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.46.1, tier: byte; tokens 1-4 of 12) opens on two suffix-conjugation verbs with freshly named subjects, turning from the first-person divine speech of MT 45:22-24 and the second-person summons of הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ (oshb:Isa.45.20, tier: byte) to a third-person tableau of Babylon's gods -- the ruled explicit scene-shift class (§2a), unique as a run (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier). So the front seam is warranted from its onset side and the row's cut is right. The row as shipped splices at MT 46:1 only נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם עֲמוּס֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.46.1, tier: byte; tokens 9-10 of 12) and מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (oshb:Isa.46.1, tier: byte; tokens 11-12 of 12) -- the finding's 'only Hebrew spliced' undercounts by one run, neither run being the onset -- never splices the verse-initial onset, and neither its prose nor its boundary_evidence_refs carries MT 45:25 (verified programmatically against the shipped row), so the seam's preceding edge is uncharacterised and the front-seam warrant rides on the WEB quotation alone. The filed finding weighed both edges (onset unengaged, preceding close uncited); the complete test re-derives it unchanged and agrees with the prior adjudication's rule. A byte-unengaged, one-edged warrant on a byte-sound seam, more than a mechanical slip under the pointed-splice mandate for boundary-relevant claims: confirm medium; field repair as proposed, no span change.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Per attested spelling, skeleton tier, verse counts: נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier) 1 verse; עֲמוּס֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier) 1; הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier) 1; הַנְּשֻׂאִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier) 3, Isa.2.13, Isa.45.20, Isa.46.3, where the 45:20 site is הַנֹּֽשְׂאִים֙ (oshb:Isa.45.20, byte tier; token 9 of 17, an active-sense participle inside the preceding row's span) and 2:13 is וְהַנִּשָּׂאִ֑ים (oshb:Isa.2.13, byte tier), a differently pointed participle of the same skeleton. The row's 'plene and defective spellings each standing in exactly 1 verse' is true only if its object is the vav-plene/defective pair on the second root, עֲמוּס֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier) against הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier); placed directly after four cited forms the sentence never says so, and under the four-form reading it is false by a factor of three, with the undisclosed recurrence sitting just across the row's own front seam at 45:20 (a skeleton-tier straddle with different pointing, not byte-true, so it argues for disclosure, not restructuring). current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh vocative opens this row: “Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, that have been carried from their birth, that have been carried from the womb.” (web:Isa.46.3), שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier), turning from the idols' own collapse (web:Isa.46.1-Isa.46.2) to Yahweh's own first-person carry-claim, “Even to old age I am he, and even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear. Yes, I will carry, and will deliver.” (web:Isa.46.4) -- וַאֲנִ֣י אֶשָּׂ֔א (oshb:Isa.46.4, byte tier) answers the very carry/bear root that named the idols' load, a deliberate contrast rather than a seam; the rescue root at Isa.46.2 is likewise answered here, וַאֲמַלֵּֽט (oshb:Isa.46.4), skeleton tier (sweep: 7 verses book-wide), undisclosed at this row's own front seam until now. The comparison challenge “To whom will you compare me, and consider my equal, and compare me, as if we were the same?” (web:Isa.46.5) and the self-declaration “Remember the former things of old; for I am God, and there is no other. I am God, and there is none like me.” (web:Isa.46.9), אָנֹכִ֥י אֵל֙ וְאֵ֣ין ע֔וֹד (oshb:Isa.46.9, byte tier), carry the disputation forward through the appeal opening web:Isa.46.8 and the Cyrus prediction “I call a ravenous bird from the east, the man of my counsel from a far country. Yes, I have spoken. I will also bring it to pass. I have planned. I will also do it.” (web:Isa.46.11) with no fresh addressee onset at either point. The row closes on a second imperative address, “Listen to me, you stubborn-hearted, who are far from righteousness!” (web:Isa.46.12) -- שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֖י (oshb:Isa.46.12) -- matching the opening's שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.46.3) at the accent-stripped tier, though the two summonses carry DIFFERENT vocatives -- אַבִּ֣ירֵי לֵ֑ב (oshb:Isa.46.12, byte tier) here against בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier) at the opening -- which is the ground on which a repeated summons with a changed addressee closes a bracket rather than opening a fresh unit; the setumah terminating Isa.46.11 (single-witness, tier-3) marks a division at Isa.46.11|Isa.46.12 as corroboration for that reading, not as a driver for it, before the closing promise “I bring my righteousness near. It is not far off, and my salvation will not wait. I will grant salvation to Zion, my glory to Israel.” (web:Isa.46.13), the row's own closing verse before a fresh address to a new addressee opens at web:Isa.47.1.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival cut would open a fresh row at the appeal opening Isa.46.8 rather than reading it as bracketed inside the wider disputation running from Isa.46.3 to Isa.46.12.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-collated: שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֖י אַבִּ֣ירֵי לֵ֑ב (oshb:Isa.46.12, byte tier; tokens 1-4 of 6) against שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier; tokens 1-4 of 14). The summons שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier) recurs at byte tier only at Isa.51.7, while at accent-stripped tier it stands in 4 verses (Isa.46.3, 46.12, 51.1, 51.7): the row's two summonses match at accent-stripped tier and differ at byte tier, as the row says. Marks (single witness): SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.46.11 (a K/Q-bearing verse) and SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.46.7, so both candidate cuts sit after a mark and the tier-3 layer does not discriminate. The 46:12 onset is a verse-initial repeated summons plus a new plural vocative, the same signal class the row drives its own front seam on at 46:3 and the following row drives at רְדִ֣י וּשְׁבִ֣י (oshb:Isa.47.1, byte tier); the 46:8 onset זִכְרוּ זֹ֖את (oshb:Isa.46.8, byte tier) with פוֹשְׁעִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.46.8, byte tier; token 5 of 7, a plural addressee in WEB) is an imperative onset too but lacks the repeated formula, and the row itself reports no onset there. So strongest_rejected_alternative names the rival the row's own prose rates weaker and omits the one it concedes: a mandated-field disclosure defect. The bracket-closing ground is argued from bytes and stays a legitimate reading, so the boundary is not impugned here (span_change false); the finding's 48:1 addressee claim lies outside this slice, unverified, and nothing turns on it. Confirm at medium.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh messenger formula opens this span at web:Isa.50.1, “Yahweh says, “Where is the bill of your mother’s divorce, with which I have put her away? Or to which of my creditors have I sold you? Behold, you were sold for your iniquities, and your mother was put away for your transgressions.”, in pointed form כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֵ֣י זֶ֠ה סֵ֣פֶר כְּרִית֤וּת אִמְּכֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שִׁלַּחְתִּ֔יהָ א֚וֹ מִ֣י מִנּוֹשַׁ֔י אֲשֶׁר מָכַ֥רְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם ל֑וֹ הֵ֤ן בַּעֲוֺנֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ נִמְכַּרְתֶּ֔ם וּבְפִשְׁעֵיכֶ֖ם שֻׁלְּחָ֥ה אִמְּכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.50.1, tier: byte), turning to an interrogative, self-vindicating form distinct from the declarative deliverance promise that precedes it: a chain of rhetorical questions continues at web:Isa.50.2, “Why, when I came, was there no one? When I called, why was there no one to answer? Is my hand shortened at all, that it can’t redeem? Or have I no power to deliver? Behold, at my rebuke I dry up the sea. I make the rivers a wilderness. Their fish stink because there is no water, and die of thirst.” pointed מַדּ֨וּעַ בָּ֜אתִי וְאֵ֣ין אִ֗ישׁ קָרָֽאתִי֮ וְאֵ֣ין עוֹנֶה֒ הֲקָצ֨וֹר קָצְרָ֤ה יָדִי֙ מִפְּד֔וּת וְאִם אֵֽין בִּ֥י כֹ֖חַ לְהַצִּ֑יל הֵ֣ן בְּגַעֲרָתִ֞י אַחֲרִ֣יב יָ֗ם אָשִׂ֤ים נְהָרוֹת֙ מִדְבָּ֔ר תִּבְאַ֤שׁ דְּגָתָם֙ מֵאֵ֣ין מַ֔יִם וְתָמֹ֖ת בַּצָּמָֽא (oshb:Isa.50.2, tier: byte), denying any incapacity to save, and the span closes at web:Isa.50.3, “I clothe the heavens with blackness. I make sackcloth their covering.””, pointed אַלְבִּ֥ישׁ שָׁמַ֖יִם קַדְר֑וּת וְשַׂ֖ק אָשִׂ֥ים כְּסוּתָֽם (oshb:Isa.50.3, tier: byte), on a demonstration of that power. Immediately before this span's onset, a parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness) sits at oshb:Isa.49.26. A SAMEKH mark (single-witness) closes this span itself, at oshb:Isa.50.3. This span's own divine first-person speech closes at oshb:Isa.50.3, and the next unit turns at web:Isa.50.4 to a fronted divine title with a first-person recipient, אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה נָ֤תַן לִי֙ (oshb:Isa.50.4, tier: byte), a form change both witnesses render alike; the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.50.3 is single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only, and is not the driver for this back seam.

The shipped strongest_rejected_alternative weighs only the unit_type tag ('Tagging this span salvation_oracle ... was considered and set aside ...', verified verbatim) and no rival span, merge or split is tested in any field; the four neighbouring rows visible in this slice each name a rival span, so the finding's batch-wide claim holds for every row I can see (the full batch is outside this slice). The field's mandated function, rival cuts disclosed, goes undischarged: a defective warrant component rather than a boundary defect, and an absent rival is no lesser shortfall than a mis-named one, so medium is the right tier. current_row.boundary_rationale: A setumah paragraph mark (single-witness, tier-3; oshb:Isa.52.12) closes immediately before this row's own opening, where a presentative particle, a third-person verb, and a first-person possessive suffix on the servant noun open the row together: הִנֵּ֥ה יַשְׂכִּ֖יל עַבְדִּ֑י (oshb:Isa.52.13, byte tier), “Behold, my servant will deal wisely. He will be exalted and lifted up, and will be very high.” (web:Isa.52.13). The description that follows shifts person twice more before the row's own close: a second-person masculine-singular address, עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ (oshb:Isa.52.14, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse), gives way in turn to the third person again, עָלָ֛יו (oshb:Isa.52.15, byte tier); the turn to direct address at web:Isa.52.14 is itself a marked person-change, disclosed here as a live internal consideration rather than adjudicated as a further seam. The row's own close instead follows a different person-shift, at the next verse, where a communal first-person-plural voice takes over — לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ (oshb:Isa.53.1, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse at every tier), “Who has believed our message? To whom has Yahweh’s arm been revealed?” (web:Isa.53.1).
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival construal keeps web:Isa.52.13-Isa.53.12 open as one undivided song rather than isolating this row, since no explicit frame-formula comparable to a hoy or koh-amar onset marks a fresh oracle boundary before web:Isa.53.1's report voice begins.

current_row.device_notes: The servant's identity stays undecided at this row; the unnamed-figure reading is one of several referent options attested across the book's servant census, and the row does not adjudicate among a prophetic, Israel-corporate, or another candidate. No royal-messenger or narrator handoff interrupts the divine voice across web:Isa.52.13-Isa.52.15. Two further echoes reach across this row's own close without disturbing it. An arm-noun echo links וּזְר֥וֹעַ (oshb:Isa.53.1) to זְר֣וֹעַ קָדְשׁ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.52.10, byte tier; outside this row) at word-bound skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses book-wide: oshb:Isa.51.9, oshb:Isa.52.10, oshb:Isa.63.12) or, allowing a prefixed match, at a wider prefix-tolerant tier (sweep: 6 verses, adding oshb:Isa.44.12, oshb:Isa.53.1, oshb:Isa.62.8); the chain runs from a verse before this row's own front seam to one past its close and does not argue against the close itself. A weaker hearing echo joins שָׁמְע֖וּ (oshb:Isa.52.15) to לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ (oshb:Isa.53.1) at only a three-letter consonantal-root tier (sweep: 30 verses book-wide) — a root-level echo, not a byte-true device, and likewise not a challenge to the seam.

items.claim: The hearing-echo digit is bound to the wrong count object: the row names a three-letter consonantal-root tier and cites 'sweep: 30 verses book-wide', but the three-letter root sweeps to 84 verses; 30 is the count for a four-letter string that does not occur in one of the two cited sites, so no sweep in the row backs the echo it is offered for.
items.proposed_change: Field repair only: replace '(sweep: 30 verses book-wide)' with the three-letter root's own digit and unit (sweep: 84 verses book-wide, contiguous consonantal substring), or re-name the count object to the form the 30 actually counts.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-swept with the count object named each time. The three-letter consonantal root shared by שָׁמְע֖וּ (oshb:Isa.52.15, byte tier) and לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ (oshb:Isa.53.1, byte tier), swept as the skeleton שמע (skeleton tier), stands as a contiguous consonantal substring in 84 verses book-wide (sweep: 84 verses; 92 token occurrences), as a whole word-bound token in 10 verses (sweep: 10 verses) and token-initially in 51 verses (sweep: 51 verses). The four-letter skeleton שמעו (skeleton tier) of the first site sweeps to exactly 30 verses (sweep: 30 verses), and the second site's skeleton לשמעתנו (skeleton tier) contains the three-letter root but not the four-letter string, so the 30-verse object cannot contain oshb:Isa.53.1 at all. The row's device_notes bind '(sweep: 30 verses book-wide)' to 'a three-letter consonantal-root tier': the digit is real but belongs to a different count object, and no sweep in the row backs the echo as offered - the finding re-derives in full. The claim sits in device_notes, is explicitly 'not a challenge to the seam', and the row's seam drivers (הִנֵּ֥ה יַשְׂכִּ֖יל עַבְדִּ֑י at oshb:Isa.52.13, byte tier; לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ at oshb:Isa.53.1, byte tier) are untouched, so this is a defective digit claim that is not load-bearing: medium confirmed. Either repair named in the proposal is byte-sound.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens at a fresh feminine-singular imperative address to a new, personified addressee: רָנִּ֥י עֲקָרָ֖ה לֹ֣א יָלָ֑דָה (oshb:Isa.54.1, byte tier), “Sing, barren, you who didn’t give birth!” (web:Isa.54.1) — replacing the servant's own speech-world of web:Isa.52.13-Isa.53.12 with a Zion-as-wife oracle. Rather than one recurring formula, the chapter's divine-speech signatures resolve into separate objects, spliced on their own terms. The verb-plus-tetragrammaton signature אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.1, byte tier; sweep: 5 verses book-wide) ends this row's own opening verse. A distinct object, naming God rather than the divine name, אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ (oshb:Isa.54.6, byte tier), ends web:Isa.54.6. A further pair interposes a participial epithet between verb and name — אָמַ֥ר גֹּאֲלֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.8, byte tier) and אָמַ֥ר מְרַחֲמֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.10, byte tier). A separate postpositive formula, נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.17, byte tier), closes the chapter on its own census. No fresh addressee or scene change accompanies any of these signatures, so the row runs to its own chapter boundary at web:Isa.54.17, immediately before a distinct invitation cry opens web:Isa.55.1.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative slices this row into shorter stanzas at its internal divine-speech signatures — the God-noun variant closing web:Isa.54.6, the two epithet-interposed forms closing web:Isa.54.8 and web:Isa.54.10, and the postpositive formula closing web:Isa.54.17 — since they are distinct closing signatures in their own right; this row instead treats them as internal refrains inside a sustained address rather than fresh frame onsets, since no addressee or scene change accompanies any of them.

current_row.device_notes: A single-witness sweep of the disclosure layers across oshb:Isa.54.1-Isa.54.17 finds a setumah paragraph mark (tier-3) bracketing the address at oshb:Isa.53.12, oshb:Isa.54.8, oshb:Isa.54.10, and oshb:Isa.54.17 — wide intervals rather than at the signature closings individually, corroborating a longer reading over a finer one without excluding a more granular decision; a paseq seg stands at oshb:Isa.54.2 (single-witness, count-only, no position within the verse claimed); and a ketiv/qere pair sits at oshb:Isa.54.16 (byte tier, single-witness), the unpointed ketiv הן running immediately into the pointed qere הִנֵּ֤ה in the source bytes. The qadosh-Israel title at קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.54.5, byte tier) recurs at accent-stripped tier only in the prefixed form heading web:Isa.55.5, a device that argues some continuity across the seam between web:Isa.54.17 and web:Isa.55.1 despite the fresh invitation-cry onset there. A second, undisclosed onset stands inside the chapter without moving its seams: רָנִּ֥י עֲקָרָ֖ה לֹ֣א יָלָ֑דָה (oshb:Isa.54.1, byte tier) and עֲנִיָּ֥ה סֹעֲרָ֖ה לֹ֣א נֻחָ֑מָה (oshb:Isa.54.11, byte tier) carry an identical four-token accent contour over a vocative-plus-negative-plus-qatal shape; the second addresses the same feminine addressee as the earlier one, so it is disclosed here as a live internal vocative rather than read as a fresh scene. This row already spans its chapter's full seventeen verses, so its confidence sits at the medium_low ceiling the campaign holds for whole-chapter units rather than at a level implying a fresh defect.

items.claim: The parashah characterization is contradicted by the inventory the row itself cites: three of the four setumah sites fall precisely on this row's own named signature closings, which are also three of the four cut points of the rival the row rejects, so the layer corroborates the finer reading rather than 'a longer reading over a finer one'.
items.proposed_change: Field repair only: state that the mark sites coincide with three of the four rival cut points and that the layer therefore supplies no tier-3 corroboration for the longer reading, dropping the 'wide intervals' and 'corroborating a longer reading over a finer one' clauses.
items.adjudicator_grounds: The single-witness inventory re-derives exactly as the finding states: SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.53.12, oshb:Isa.54.8, oshb:Isa.54.10 and oshb:Isa.54.17, and no petuchah or setumah at any other verse of oshb:Isa.54.1-Isa.54.17 (the row's four cited sites are the only sites). The closings re-collate at byte tier: oshb:Isa.54.8 ends on אָמַ֥ר גֹּאֲלֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.8, byte tier), oshb:Isa.54.10 on אָמַ֥ר מְרַחֲמֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.10, byte tier), oshb:Isa.54.17 on נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.17, byte tier) - three of the four cut points the row's own strongest_rejected_alternative assigns to the rival - while the fourth rival cut, after אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ (oshb:Isa.54.6, byte tier), and the opening signature אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.1, byte tier; sweep: 5 verses at byte tier, re-derived) carry no mark. The interval oshb:Isa.54.8 to oshb:Isa.54.10 is two verses. So 'wide intervals rather than at the signature closings individually' is false on the row's own cited data, and 'corroborating a longer reading over a finer one' inverts what the layer shows: every mark inside the chapter falls on a rival cut point and none falls anywhere else, so the layer (tier-3 weak corroboration under owner law, never a driver either way) aligns with the finer reading, not the longer one. The seam driver is the byte-grounded vocative onset רָנִּ֥י עֲקָרָ֖ה לֹ֣א יָלָ֑דָה (oshb:Isa.54.1, byte tier), untouched by this defect; the mark claim is defective but not load-bearing - medium confirmed. Field repair as proposed; no span change (the layer's alignment with the rival is corroboration only and cannot itself move a seam).

items.claim: 'the prefixed form heading web:Isa.55.5' is byte-false: the prefixed title stands as the fourteenth of that verse's seventeen tokens, and the verse is headed by a different word.
items.proposed_change: Field repair only: replace 'heading web:Isa.55.5' with 'standing inside web:Isa.55.5' (or a neutral 'at web:Isa.55.5').
items.adjudicator_grounds: oshb:Isa.55.5 carries 17 tokens and opens on הֵ֣ן (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier); the prefixed title וְלִקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier) occupies token positions 14-15, preceded by יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier). So 'the prefixed form heading web:Isa.55.5' is byte-false as a position claim. The underlying tier claim re-derives: קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.54.5, byte tier) collates against oshb:Isa.55.5 at accent_stripped tier only, not at byte tier, exactly as the row says. The defect is confined to the position word in device_notes, on a continuity device the row already subordinates to the invitation-cry onset at web:Isa.55.1, so it is not load-bearing for the row's own seams - but it is not inert either: read as written it would put a verse-initial divine title at the head of the very verse whose seam status (Isa.55.4|Isa.55.5 against Isa.55.5|Isa.55.6) is contested in the neighbouring rows, so it is a byte-false factual claim rather than a mechanical slip. Medium confirmed; the proposed one-word repair cures it.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens where an invitation cry addresses a fresh audience: ה֤וֹי כָּל צָמֵא֙ (oshb:Isa.55.1, byte tier), “Hey! Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters!” (web:Isa.55.1). This hoy functions as an invitation, not a woe-oracle onset and not the divine self-exclamation class attested elsewhere in the book; the address moves from the Zion-as-wife addressee of web:Isa.54.1-Isa.54.17 to the thirsty, moneyless audience of web:Isa.55.1-Isa.55.2, held in the masculine plural through אָזְנְכֶם֙ and נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם (oshb:Isa.55.3, byte tier). The row closes where that plural narrows down to one addressee: the verb תֵדַע֙ turns singular early in the verse, and it closes on the singular suffixes of אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ and פֵאֲרָֽךְ (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier), so the whole verse runs masculine singular, a turn neither witness's English marks, since both render every surrounding pronoun the same way; a singular-you suffix stands in exactly one of the seven verses oshb:Isa.55.1-Isa.55.7, and this is that verse. Immediately afterward, the address returns to the masculine plural of the row's own opening rather than staying singular: דִּרְשׁ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.55.6, byte tier) is the same plural-imperative form-class as לְכ֣וּ (oshb:Isa.55.1, byte tier) and וּלְכ֣וּ (oshb:Isa.55.3, byte tier), so what changes at oshb:Isa.55.6 is the addressee's return to the plural, not the imperative's grammatical shape. A setumah paragraph mark (single-witness, tier-3) closes at oshb:Isa.54.17, this row's own front-seam predecessor, and again at oshb:Isa.55.5, this row's own final verse.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative keeps web:Isa.55.1-Isa.55.13 undivided rather than cutting between web:Isa.55.5 and web:Isa.55.6, since both halves share the chapter's sustained direct address; this row instead follows the addressee's return to the masculine plural at web:Isa.55.6, after the singular turn disclosed at web:Isa.55.5, as sufficient warrant for a fresh seam.

current_row.device_notes: This row's own instance of the qadosh-Israel title, וְלִקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier), echoes its earlier occurrence at oshb:Isa.54.5 only at accent-stripped tier — the prefix attached here changes the leading bytes, so the two meet where cantillation is stripped away rather than at the letter-for-letter tier. The device still bridges the seam between web:Isa.54.17 and web:Isa.55.1, even though the fresh invitation-cry onset is treated as the stronger tier-1 signal for the cut.

items.claim: The rear-seam driver is corroborated by a claim about translation behaviour -- 'a turn neither witness's English marks, since both render every surrounding pronoun the same way' -- which is tier-4 metadata used as corroboration and which presupposes a second English witness that the staged corpus does not carry.
items.proposed_change: Field repair only: delete the translation-rendering clause and let the singular-turn stand on the pointed bytes and the seven-verse suffix sweep already in the field.
items.adjudicator_grounds: The Hebrew the sentence supports re-derives in full: oshb:Isa.55.5 runs masculine singular from תֵדַע֙ through יְדָע֖וּךָ אֵלֶ֣יךָ to אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ and פֵאֲרָֽךְ (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier); oshb:Isa.55.2 closes on נַפְשְׁכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.55.2, byte tier) and oshb:Isa.55.3 carries אָזְנְכֶם֙, נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם and לָכֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.55.3, byte tier), all plural; oshb:Isa.55.1, oshb:Isa.55.4, oshb:Isa.55.6 and oshb:Isa.55.7 carry no second-person suffix (oshb:Isa.55.1 and oshb:Isa.55.6 carry plural imperatives only), so 'exactly one of the seven verses' is true.
